pr.title: Name a drawer's session roles fixer and reviewer
pr.head: 4860413180fc73dad9f17f12d86c51e776108910

summary: Projector's panel is the area Claude Code draws above the prompt. It lists the pull requests the session fixes or reviews, one line each, and clicking a pull request's number opens a drawer under that line with more about it.

Two places in the panel used the word reviewing for different facts. The row shows reviewing when the pull request carries the reviewing label, which a Projector review adds while it runs, in any session. The drawer's first line also said reviewing, but there it meant the session's role: this session is subscribed to review the pull request, whether or not a review is running. While a review ran, the two words sat one above the other and looked redundant. After the review published, the label left and the drawer's word stayed, which read as a contradiction.

This change makes the drawer name the session by its role as a noun: fixer, reviewer, or fixer and reviewer, in the same blue and orange as before. Only the words drawn in the drawer change. The role values inside the mod stay fixing and reviewing, so the toast a dismissal shows still reads stopped fixing and reviewing owner/repo#7.

cards.title: Which word means what
cards.html:
WhereWordMeans
RowreviewingThe pull request carries the reviewing label: a review is running now, in any session.
DrawerreviewerThis session is subscribed to review the pull request.
DrawerfixerThis session is subscribed to fix the pull request's review findings.
Dismissal toaststopped fixing and reviewingThe roles the session stopped, as verbs. Unchanged.

groups.title: The drawer's role words
groups.kicker: A map from each role to the noun the drawer draws for it
intro: A role is what the session does for a pull request, held in the mod as the value fixing or reviewing. The drawer's first line, its facts line, starts with the session's roles, each in its own color, joined by and. That line is the only place the panel draws a role's name.

The change adds ROLE_NAMES, which maps each role to its noun, and the facts line now draws ROLE_NAMES[role] where it drew the role value. Colors still come from ROLE_COLORS, keyed by the same role values.

files.note: The panel's mod. Adds ROLE_NAMES and draws it on the drawer's facts line.

checks.text: The comment above the map gives the reason for a noun: it keeps the session's role from reading as the reviewing label on the row above.

The facts line is the only text that renders a role's name. The dismissal toast still joins the raw role values, so it keeps the verbs. Checked by searching the mod for every place that renders a role.

files.note: The drawer tests now expect fixer, reviewer, and fixer and reviewer with their colors.

checks.text: The tests catch a wrong label. With ROLE_NAMES swapped so that a fixer reads reviewer, 7 drawer tests failed, and all 227 passed again with the head's map.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The panel's guide and the theme plan name the new words
intro: docs/plugins.md describes the panel. The change updates the example panel, the paragraph about the drawer, and the note about older watcher scripts to use fixer and reviewer. It adds a sentence that says how the drawer's reviewer differs from the row's reviewing label.

The draft panel-themes plan, which would let each panel color follow a theme, keeps its theme keys fixing and reviewing, named after the role values. Its role table now says those keys color fixer and reviewer in the drawer.
